questions.stem: Why must the electrolyte be molten or dissolved in solution for electrolysis to work?

options.text: So the electrolyte can conduct heat more efficiently
So the ions are free to move and carry the electrical current
So the electrodes can dissolve into the electrolyte
So the electrons can flow through the liquid

questions.explanation: In a solid ionic compound, the ions are held in fixed positions in the lattice and cannot move. When the compound is melted or dissolved, the ions become free to move towards the electrodes, allowing them to carry the electrical current through the electrolyte.

questions.stem: What process occurs at the cathode during electrolysis?
questions.explanation: At the cathode (negative electrode), reduction occurs. Positive ions (cations) are attracted to the cathode, where they gain electrons. This is remembered by the mnemonic RED CAT -- REDuction at the CAThode. For example, Pb²⁺ + 2e⁻ → Pb.
